subject: SCIENCE
title: Motion from a Reference Point
objective: Describe position and motion relative to a named reference point.
introduction: Milo marks a cone as a reference point; the ball moves from beside it to farther away. How can Maxine describe that motion?

vocabulary.definition: An exact spot used to mark where something is.
A change in position compared with a reference point over time.
A named object or spot used for comparing position or motion.

items.prompt: Milo compares a ball with a cone before and after it rolls. Which statement about motion is true?

options.text: Motion is a change in position relative to a reference point over time.
No reference point is needed
Use color as position
Motion means an object changes material.

items.explanation: To tell whether the ball moved, compare its position with the cone over time. Color and material changes do not describe this motion.

items.prompt: A ball starts beside a cone and rolls away from it. Which example shows motion?

options.text: The ball moves away from the cone
The ball stays in a box all day
The cone changes color
The ball feels happy

items.explanation: The ball changes position compared with the cone, so it is moving. Staying still, changing color, or feeling happy does not show motion.

items.prompt: Maxine wants to describe a cart’s motion. Which piece of information is NOT needed for a position comparison?

options.text: A cart moves past a tree
A cart is beside a cone
No reference point is named
A cart is farther from a box

items.explanation: A reference point such as a tree, cone, or box is needed for comparison. Without one, a position change cannot be described clearly.

items.prompt: A ball changes from beside a cone to far from it. Relative to the cone, what happened?

options.text: It became heavier
It moved
It changed color
It became louder

items.explanation: The ball’s position changed compared with the cone, so it moved. Weight, color, and loudness do not tell whether its position changed.

items.prompt: Milo says, “The book is beside the box.” What does that sentence describe?

options.text: The book’s position compared with a box
The book moves because it wants to
The book is happy
The book changes into a box

items.explanation: “Beside the box” names a reference point and the book’s position relative to it. Feelings and wishes are not position evidence.
